Atomically removes eligible pending notifications while retaining the subscription. Returns the registration and a u32 removal count, never the removed payloads. Stops before a filter event. Publishes an immutable semantic snapshot of the supplied T to current subscribers, without recursively executing a consumer. Embedded references retain identity. Creates a dynamic subscription, or updates the supplied registration without creating another queue. Each stable row associates a typed source with a compatible event from the common catalog. Sharing the same registration between consumers shares its queue; create independent registrations for broadcast delivery. None, null and unwired inputs follow the documented FROG adapter contract, not a measured NI compatibility claim.

Solves residual R(t,X,dX)=0 using genuine three-stage implicit Radau IIA order 5 and nonlinear Newton solves. A residual is not an explicit derivative and Radau is not BDF. Formula declares residual equations, state names, derivative names and time. State and derivative outputs share Times and shape [time,state]. Regular index-1 DAE baseline; no general higher-index guarantee. X0/dX0 must be consistent; no silent correction. Defaults t0=0,tf=10,atol=[.001],rtol=[.001],initial_step=.01,min_step=1e-8,max_step=1. Tolerance arrays have length 1 (broadcast) or N, nonnegative and not both zero per component. Steps satisfy 0<min_step<max_step with initial_step in bounds. Real f64 coupled systems, not element-wise batch lifting. Vectors are rank 1; matrices and multistate trajectories are actual rank-2 Arrays, not nominal Matrix transport. Values[row,column] is state column at Times[row]. Explicit exception: Linear nth Order Numeric returns only x(t) as a rank-1 Array, without its derivatives. Borrowed Variant user data is opaque to the f64 ODE state profile and may preserve exact common typed payloads, including I128/U128 lexical values, without numeric conversion. No complex transport, implicit batch, dimensional broadcasting or scalar lifting. Formula and FROG Reference are explicitly selected persisted identities sharing one palette artwork. Common connector IDs survive switching instances. ODE Solver and DAE use error in/out clusters; the legacy RK4, CK, Euler and linear functions retain error:i32 (zero means success). ticks:u32 is elapsed calculation milliseconds, not step count or simulated time. Invalid preconditions return empty results; a stopped integration retains accepted rows with an explicit nonzero diagnostic. Resource limits, cancellation, invalid references, nonfinite values and unavailable methods never become plausible zero-valued success. Classic LabVIEW connector documentation and mathematical algorithms; no measured NI runtime parity or confirmed NXG graphical signatures. Local execution uses the existing immutable authored graph and its owned Highlight worker, through Play with or without the bulb. The public-source LLVM compiled target corridor does not admit these aggregate signatures yet and rejects them explicitly; there is no substituted provider.

Counts unordered selections of k distinct elements among n. U32 inputs produce an F64 coefficient and a separate I32 status. FROG defines k>n as coefficient=0,error=0; boundaries k=0 or k=n give 1. Finite large coefficients may round. Overflow gives +Infinity,error=2; ordinary success gives error=0. Formula: C(n,k)=n!/(k!*(n-k)!) for k<=n; 0 for k>n. Example: C(5,2)=10; C(5,3)=10; C(5,0)=1.

Returns a Boolean primality result for an I64 integer. Every n<2, including negative values, is False; the magnitude is not substituted. The FROG contract is deterministic on the entire I64 range, not a probabilistic guess. Formula: true iff n is a prime integer >= 2. Example: Check Prime(-7)=False; Check Prime(97)=True; Check Prime(561)=False.

Evaluates the finite rational convergent A[0]/(B[0]+A[1]/(B[1]+...)), using every coefficient. Required A and B are nonempty rank-one F64 arrays of equal length with finite coefficients. Result is F64 with a separate I32 status. Empty/unequal arrays, nonfinite coefficients or a final zero denominator give NaN,error=1; overflow gives an overflow indication. Intermediate zero denominators are not automatically invalid: A=[1,1],B=[2,0] gives 0. This A[0] convention is FROG; NI equation indexing remains unconfirmed. It evaluates supplied coefficients, not a scalar-to-coefficients conversion. Formula: A[0]/(B[0]+A[1]/(B[1]+...+A[m-1]/B[m-1])). Computes n! for an I32 integer, returning F64. FROG defines 0!=1, negative n as NaN with a domain indication and n>=171 as +Infinity with overflow. Computes the nonnegative greatest common divisor of two I32 integers. FROG defines gcd(x,0)=abs(x) and gcd(0,0)=0; a magnitude of 2^31 is an I32 overflow, reported without wraparound or a usable result. Formula: gcd(abs(x),abs(y)). Example: GCD(-48,18)=6; GCD(0,0)=0.

Computes the nonnegative least common multiple of two I32 integers in I64 arithmetic. Returns zero if either input is zero; the widened result can exceed I32 without overflow. Formula: 0 if x==0 or y==0, otherwise abs((x/gcd(x,y))*y). Example: LCM(-12,18)=36; LCM(0,18)=0.

Counts ordered selections of k distinct elements among n, without replacement. Inputs n and k are U32; output nPk is F64. FROG defines k=0 as 1, including (0,0), and k>n as 0. Factors the magnitude of an I64 integer into a rank-one I64 array. Returns both Airy functions on independent real F64 outputs ai and bi. Ai decreases and Bi increases for positive arguments; an overflow of Bi does not invalidate a calculable Ai. At r=0: Ai=0.3550280538878172, Bi=0.6149266274460007. No order input or derivative outputs. Standard Airy functions are not even; this adapter deliberately uses |x|. Formula: Ai(r), Bi(r). Example: Ai(1)=0.1352924163128814; Bi(1)=1.2074235949528713.

Cylindrical Bessel function of the first kind, real order v (fractional and signed orders accepted). At r=0: 1 for v=0; 0 for positive v or negative integers; singular for negative noninteger v. Formula: J_v(r). Example: J_0(1)=0.7651976865579666.

Cylindrical Bessel function of the second kind (Neumann), real order v. Requires r>0; r=0 is singular. Negative and fractional orders are accepted. Formula: Y_v(r). Example: Y_0(1)=0.08825696421567696.

Modified Bessel function of the first kind, real order v. Public results are unscaled. At r=0: 1 for v=0; 0 for positive v or negative integers; singular for negative noninteger v. Negative noninteger orders do not use absolute order. Formula: I_v(r). Example: I_0(1)=1.2660658777520084.

Modified Bessel function of the second kind, signed integer order n. K_-n=K_n. The supplied Kv(x) glyph is preserved; its connector remains integer. Requires r>0; r=0 is singular. Public results are unscaled; representable subnormals are retained. Formula: K_n(r). Example: K_0(1)=0.4210244382407083.

Spherical Bessel function of the first kind, signed integer order n; j_0(r)=sin(r)/r. Distinct from cylindrical J. At r=0: 1 for n=0; 0 for n>0; singular for n<0. Negative orders use spherical reflection relations. Formula: sqrt(pi/(2*r))*J_(n+1/2)(r). Example: j_0(1)=0.8414709848078965.

Spherical Bessel function of the second kind, signed integer order n; y_0(r)=-cos(r)/r. Distinct from cylindrical Y. At r=0: singular for n>=0; 1 for n=-1; 0 for n<=-2, using negative-order reflection. Formula: sqrt(pi/(2*r))*Y_(n+1/2)(r). Example: y_0(1)=-0.5403023058681398.

Evaluates Jacobi cn, dn, sn and continuous amplitude phi for real x and parameter m=k (not k squared and not the modulus). Domain 0<=k<=1. phi is in radians and retains its periods: phi(u+2K)=phi(u)+pi. At k=0: cos(u),1,sin(u),u; at k=1: sech(u),sech(u),tanh(u),2 atan(tanh(u/2)). At x=1,k=.25: cn=.568568998095171, dn=.911492005669132, sn=.822635578129862, phi=.966031052636614. Both inputs f64 required without defaults. ni_documented_real_v1 uses u=abs(x), never abs(k), abs(v) or abs(result); standard_real_v1 keeps signed x. NI-G documentation; NI/NXG runtime parity unmeasured.

Evaluates the normalized parabolic cylinder function Dv(x), the Weber solution with Dv(z)~z^v exp(-z*z/4) at positive infinity. v is a real order: negative and fractional values are accepted without rounding or abs(v). Exactly one output Dv(x), no derivative. D0(1)=D1(1)=.778800783071405; D2(0)=-1 and D2(1)=0; D0.5(1)=.842203244069840. Finite x and v define a real function; machine limits are diagnosed separately. Both inputs f64 required without defaults. ni_documented_real_v1 uses u=abs(x), never abs(k), abs(v) or abs(result); standard_real_v1 keeps signed x. NI-G documentation; NI/NXG runtime parity unmeasured.

Evaluates real Chi(abs(x)) with Euler gamma plus log(q) normalization. Chi(0)=-Infinity with singularity; Chi(1)=0.8378669409802082. A scaled algorithm preserves finite Chi(717).
Evaluates real Ci(abs(x)), including Euler gamma plus log(q) normalization. Ci(0)=-Infinity with singularity, Ci(1)=0.3374039229009681; this is not Cin or a complex continuation.
Evaluates D(q)=-Li2(1-q)=integral(1,q,ln(t)/(t-1),dt), q=abs(x), following the NI/CVI equation. D(0)=-pi^2/6, D(1)=0 and D(2)=pi^2/12; t=1 is removable.

Evaluates E_n(q)=integral(1,infinity,exp(-q*t)/t^n,dt), q=abs(x), with required integer n>=0 and no default order. E0(q)=exp(-q)/q; E0(0) and E1(0) are +Infinity with singularity; En(0)=1/(n-1) for n>=2. E1(710) remains a representable subnormal.

Evaluates Shi(abs(x))=integral(0,abs(x),sinh(t)/t,dt). Standard Shi is odd, but this documented adapter uses abs(x): Shi(-1)=+1.0572508753757286. Shi(0)=0; a scaled algorithm preserves finite Shi(717).
Evaluates Si(x)=integral(0,x,sin(t)/t,dt) in radians with signed x. Si(0)=0, Si(-1)=-0.946083070367183 and Si(+infinity)=pi/2.

Cylindrical Hankel function. type=0 selects the first kind J+iY; type=1 selects the second kind J-iY. One complex F64 output preserves both components. Requires r>0 and type in {0,1}; r=0 is singular. This evaluates a function, not a Hankel transform. Formula: J_v(r)+i*Y_v(r) for type=0; J_v(r)-i*Y_v(r) for type=1. Example: H_0^(1)(1)=0.7651976865579666+0.08825696421567696i.

Spherical Hankel function, signed integer order n. type=0 gives j+iy; type=1 gives j-iy. One complex F64 output preserves both components. Requires r>0 and type in {0,1}; r=0 is singular for every integer order. Distinct from cylindrical H. Formula: j_n(r)+i*y_n(r) for type=0; j_n(r)-i*y_n(r) for type=1. Example: h_0^(1)(1)=0.8414709848078965-0.5403023058681398i.

Kelvin be at signed integer order n. The real component is ber and the imaginary component is bei; one complex F64 output, with real input x. At r=0: 1+0i for n=0; 0+0i otherwise. Negative orders use be_-n=(-1)^n*be_n. Formula: ber_n(r)+i*bei_n(r)=J_n(r*exp(3*pi*i/4)). Example: be_0(1)=0.9843817812130868+0.2495660400366597i.

Kelvin ke at signed integer order n. The real component is ker and the imaginary component is kei; one complex F64 output, with real input x. The order-dependent phase is retained. Requires r>0; r=0 is singular. Negative orders use ke_-n=(-1)^n*ke_n. This is neither reciprocal be nor real-axis K. Formula: ker_n(r)+i*kei_n(r)=exp(-n*pi*i/2)*K_n(r*exp(pi*i/4)). Example: ke_0(1)=0.2867062087283160-0.4949946365187199i.

Ordinary Struve H function, real order v. This is distinct from Hankel H and modified Struve L; there is no kind selector. At r=0: 0 for v>-1; 2/pi for v=-1; 0 for v=-3/2-m (integer m>=0); singular for other v<-1. Formula: H_v(r) (ordinary Struve). Example: Struve H_0(1)=0.5686566270482879.

Releases this acquired handle, including with an incoming error. Other acquired handles stay usable unless this is the last one or force destroy=True. Destruction wakes pending waits with an error. Returns the name and latest value, never a notifier reference.

Atomically publishes one typed notification and wakes eligible waiting readers. Replaces the previous value instead of enqueueing it. Equal values sent twice remain distinct emissions; every reader has its own reception state.

Reads a coherent, non-consuming snapshot: notifier name, latest uncanceled value and number of pending waits. The value is default(T) when empty; it is not a presence flag. A Multiple wait counts once per distinct watched object.

Waits for a new emission for this node instance without consuming the stored value. Ordinary waiting keeps one compact emission cursor. Ignore previous=True waits only for emissions after this call begins. Timeout -1 is unbounded, 0 polls, below -1 errors. Timed out? is also True on error.

Finishes when at least one watched notifier has an admissible emission. Returns matching reference/value arrays for ready distinct objects, in input order (FROG decision), not all input references. Generate, wait for and signal a shared Occurrence reference. A signal wakes eligible waiters without a message payload, FIFO or global consumption. Distinct Generate and Wait instances retain separate runtime identities.

Returns this node instance's occurrence reference. Repeated activations within the same executable instance reuse that reference. Distinct nodes and isolated instances remain independent. No payload or native address is editable.

Signals the supplied occurrence and makes its pending waiters eligible to resume. No application data is transferred and no acknowledgement is awaited. This is an effect even without an output terminal. An invalid reference cannot signal another resource and is diagnosed.

Suspends this execution path until an eligible signal arrives or the wait expires. An invalid reference returns timed out immediately. Timeout is signed I32 milliseconds: -1 (default) waits indefinitely, 0 checks immediately, positive values set a monotonic deadline; values below -1 are controlled argument faults. ignore previous defaults to TRUE and ignores signals before atomic registration. FALSE accepts an unseen earlier generation for this Wait instance; acknowledged signals are not replayed and multiple signals may coalesce. This is not a FIFO. Cancellation does not publish a normal timed out result.
Typed FIFO resource operations. Queue<T> is the shared access reference, not a message or a Front Panel object reference. Each message retains its complete type.

Removes and returns the head element in FIFO order. An empty queue waits cooperatively: -1 means no deadline, 0 an immediate attempt. Ordinary timeout is distinguished from invalidation and from a successfully received message. Queue<T> is an execution resource reference; element is the ordinary T value. Public FROG target compilation remains unavailable.

Adds one element at the tail. A full bounded FIFO waits cooperatively for space: timeout -1 waits indefinitely, 0 attempts immediately. Expiration inserts nothing. It never silently evicts an element; invalidation interrupts the wait with an error. Queue<T> is an execution resource reference; element is the ordinary T value. Public FROG target compilation remains unavailable.

Atomically removes the present messages and returns them in FIFO order, preserving each complete message boundary even when T itself is an Array. The queue stays valid and usable; an empty FIFO returns an empty outer array. Queue<T> is an execution resource reference; element is the ordinary T value. Public FROG target compilation remains unavailable.

Atomically evicts the oldest element only if a bounded FIFO is full, then appends the new element without waiting. The overflow element is meaningful only when overflow? is true. Ordinary Enqueue does not use this lossy behavior. Queue<T> is an execution resource reference; element is the ordinary T value. Public FROG target compilation remains unavailable.

Creates an anonymous FIFO when name is empty, or obtains an additional access to a same-application named FIFO with exactly the complete element type. The type specimen is not an inserted message. Capacity defaults to -1; an existing named capacity is preserved. Queue<T> is an execution resource reference; element is the ordinary T value. Public FROG target compilation remains unavailable.

Returns the head element without removal or reservation. An empty FIFO waits cooperatively using timeout -1 by default. A successful preview does not prevent another consumer removing that message. Queue<T> is an execution resource reference; element is the ordinary T value. Public FROG target compilation remains unavailable.

Releases this obtained access, preserving independently obtained accesses unless force destroy is true. Forced destruction invalidates all accesses and wakes waits with errors. Cleanup also executes with an incoming error. Returns the FIFO snapshot before release and never returns a queue reference. Queue<T> is an execution resource reference; element is the ordinary T value. Public FROG target compilation remains unavailable.

Reads a coherent instant snapshot: name, capacity, count and waiting operations. Preview and dequeue both count as pending removals. Elements are returned only when requested, without removal; otherwise that output is an empty array. Queue<T> is an execution resource reference; element is the ordinary T value. Public FROG target compilation remains unavailable.

Six reusable participant-barrier operations: create, wait, resize, destroy, status and validity. Rendezvous Ref has no message type. Each successful cohort belongs to one generation; later arrivals wait for a new cohort.

Creates an anonymous reusable barrier, or atomically finds the exact same-context name without resizing it. Size defaults to 2 and must be 1..INT32_MAX. Return existing prohibits creation. Upstream errors prevent allocation or lookup.

Destroys the resource and all aliases, removes its name and ends pending waits with error and timed out=True. Executes cleanup despite an upstream error, which retains priority. Returns the name, no reference and no force option. Already committed successful cohorts retain success.

Returns True for a null, destroyed, stale-incarnation or foreign-context Rendezvous reference; False for a live barrier even with no arrivals. This is not a threshold test. There is no error chain or output reference.

Atomically adds the signed size change to the current threshold; it is a delta, never an absolute size. FROG releases the entire current cohort if the lower threshold is satisfied. Nonpositive or overflowing results leave state unchanged. Upstream errors skip mutation.

Reads a coherent snapshot of name, current pending arrivals and participant threshold without arriving or reserving. The unchanged reference is forwarded. The snapshot may immediately become stale and cannot replace Wait. On error scalar defaults do not describe a valid resource.

Registers this call once in the current generation and suspends only this task until the threshold, timeout, destruction or cancellation. A completed cohort cannot release a later generation. Upstream error skips arrival and returns timed out=True. FROG timeout 0 tests arrival immediately; -1 has no deadline.

Six semaphore operations: obtain and close resource references, acquire and return counted accesses, read status and test validity. SemaphoreRef carries no message type. Reference closure and access release are distinct.

Atomically acquires one available access or suspends only the requesting task. Timeout zero is an immediate trial, minus one is infinite, and values below minus one are invalid. Executes despite upstream error. FROG v1 reports timed_out=false on actual acquisition and preserves upstream error; an ordinary timeout adds no blocking error.

Returns True for a null, closed or destroyed semaphore handle; False for a live handle, including a saturated semaphore. It is not a capacity test and does not protect against a later concurrent close. No error chain or outgoing reference is part of this connector.

Creates an independent anonymous semaphore, or obtains a distinct handle to the exact same-context name. Capacity is positive, defaults to one and never changes for an existing named resource. No access is acquired. Standard upstream-error handling prevents hidden creation.

Returns exactly one acquired access and may admit one waiter. It does not close the handle. Releasing without an acquisition is an error and cannot increase availability above capacity. Executes despite upstream error and preserves it; no OS-thread ownership is imposed.

Closes this handle and its aliases, interrupts only its pending acquisitions, and returns the semaphore name. Other handles survive normal close; force destroy invalidates all handles and waits. Executes despite upstream error. FROG v1 does not implicitly return already acquired accesses when another handle keeps the resource alive.

Returns one coherent snapshot of name, capacity, available accesses and actually suspended acquisitions without reserving or returning an access. Expired and canceled requests are removed from waiting_count. The handle is unchanged. Standard upstream-error handling applies; an invalid handle produces a diagnostic.
